newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - NOV 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - NOV 6.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--The 1997 budget is still on the table with final decisions expected today at a repeat of yesterday's meeting between Prime Minister Costas Simtis and National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou. The reason for the delay is the search for a compromise between satisfying the high revenue needs of the budget and maintaining political and social balances. Simitis appears to want the budget tabled by November 22. --The capital market's bodies yesterday warned 10 brokerage firms that it has until today to comply with the clearing house on delivery of shares or they will be banned from trading. --There will be stricter criteria for firms receiving subsidies under the state's development laws in an effort to better monitor cash flows.
--The package of new taxes which will support the 1997 budget

was decided yesterday at the Simitis-Papandoniou meeting. Reports say Simitis gave the green light for the taxation of state titles and derivatives, possible at between 8-10 percent. The real estate tax will also go ahead and final details on it will be discussed at a later meeting.
--Today's meeting will finalise the details of two bills to
support the budget: one on cutting back tax exemptions and the
other on the reduction of state expenditures.

--The delayed response of the Athens Stock Exchange in placing sanctions on firms regarding the delivery of shares has only intensified the phenomenon of share-lending between brokers. --The Commission sees an improvement in Greece's economic indiators but says that if the public deficit (as a percentage of GDP) is not reduced to 7.0 percent by mid-1997, the Commission may have to suspend Community financing. --Finance Undersecretary George Drys yesterday tabled in Parliament the names of 400 yacht and cabin cruise owners whose under-valued craft have cost the state 4.4 billion drachmas.

--Greece and Italy will miss out on Economic and Monetary Union by the year 2000 if they fail to reduce their deficits to 3 percent of GDP, sources in Brussels say. Brussels considers sanctions on countries failing to make the grade. --Better financial management of university funding is a goal for the finance ministry, sources say. --The development ministry and the Greek National Tourism Organisation (EOT) is examining a 50 billion drachma investment in Messinia.

--The government weighs internal party objections to the new budget at today's meeting. The procedures of how to impose new taxes are still undecided. --The state aspires to recoup 100 billion drachmas of the 2.2 trillion drachmas owed in Value Added Tax by state bodies and organisations and the private sector. --The governor of the National Bank is being pressured to reconsider the agreement between Calnet and the Italian firm Concretum over AGET-Heracles cement company. --The development ministry is pursuing changes to the status on rentals of business premises.
--The National Bank's goals for 1997 include selling off non financial assets and expanding its portfolio. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
